fields.description: The primary long-lived greenhouse gas produced by fossil fuel combustion, deforestation, and industrial processes, responsible for the majority of anthropogenic radiative forcing.
fields.scheme_name: E.3 Climate factors - Climate forcing agents

fields.name: k_climate-forcing-agents|2
fields.title: Fluorinated gases / hydrofluorocarbons / perfluorocarbons / sulfur hexafluoride / nitrogen trifluoride
fields.description: A group of potent synthetic greenhouse gases used in industrial applications, refrigeration, and electronics manufacturing, with very high global warming potentials and long atmospheric lifetimes.
fields.scheme_name: E.3 Climate factors - Climate forcing agents

fields.name: k_climate-forcing-agents|3
fields.title: Methane (CH₄)
fields.description: A potent short-lived greenhouse gas emitted from livestock, rice cultivation, landfills, and fossil fuel extraction, with a global warming potential far exceeding that of CO₂ over 20 years.
fields.scheme_name: E.3 Climate factors - Climate forcing agents

fields.name: k_climate-forcing-agents|4
fields.title: Nitrous oxide (N₂O)
fields.description: A greenhouse gas and ozone-depleting substance emitted primarily from agricultural soils, livestock, and nitrogen fertilisers, with a high global warming potential.
fields.scheme_name: E.3 Climate factors - Climate forcing agents

fields.name: k_climate-forcing-agents|5
fields.title: Ozone-depleting substances / chlorofluorocarbons / hydrochlorofluorocarbons / halons / carbon tetrachloride / methyl chloroform
fields.description: Chemical compounds that destroy stratospheric ozone and act as potent greenhouse gases, regulated under the Montreal Protocol due to their combined climate and health impacts.
fields.scheme_name: E.3 Climate factors - Climate forcing agents

fields.name: k_climate-forcing-agents|6
fields.title: Particulate matter (PM10) / fine particulate matter (PM2.5) / black/organic carbon / sulfate/nitrate aerosols
fields.description: Airborne particles of 10 or 2.5 micrometres or less in diameter. Fine particulate matter can include components such as black carbon and sulfate aerosols, that affect both climate and human health through respiratory and cardiovascular pathways.
fields.scheme_name: E.3 Climate factors - Climate forcing agents

fields.name: k_climate-forcing-agents|7
fields.title: Tropospheric ozone (O₃)
fields.description: A short-lived climate pollutant and air quality hazard formed by photochemical reactions between nitrogen oxides and volatile organic compounds, harmful to respiratory health.
fields.scheme_name: E.3 Climate factors - Climate forcing agents

fields.name: k_fossil-fuels|0
fields.title: (Unspecified) fossil fuels
fields.description: Fossil fuel use or combustion where the specific fuel type is not identified, used when studies refer to fossil fuels in general without distinguishing between coal, oil, or gas.

fields.name: k_fossil-fuels|1
fields.title: Coal
fields.description: A solid fossil fuel formed from ancient plant matter, the most carbon-intensive energy source and a major contributor to greenhouse gas emissions and air pollution.

fields.name: k_fossil-fuels|2
fields.title: Natural gas
fields.description: A fossil fuel composed primarily of methane, used for heating, electricity generation, and industrial processes, with lower CO₂ emissions than coal but significant methane leakage risks.

fields.name: k_fossil-fuels|3
fields.title: Oil
fields.description: A liquid fossil fuel refined into petroleum products including petrol, diesel, and jet fuel, a major source of greenhouse gas emissions from transport and industry.

fields.name: k_interventions-measures-responses|0
fields.title: Behavior / culture
fields.description: Human behaviours, social practices, and cultural norms that influence greenhouse gas emissions or shape vulnerability and resilience to climate change impacts.

fields.name: k_interventions-measures-responses|1
fields.title: Community-based
fields.description: Locally designed and led interventions that mobilise communities to address climate-health risks, drawing on local knowledge, social networks, and collective action.

fields.name: k_interventions-measures-responses|2
fields.title: Ecosystem-based
fields.description: Interventions that use the sustainable management, conservation, or restoration of ecosystems to reduce climate-related health risks and deliver co-benefits for biodiversity and human wellbeing, including urban green-blue infrastructure, coastal and marine protection, and forest and land management.

fields.name: k_interventions-measures-responses|3
fields.title: Institutional
fields.description: Actions taken by formal organisations and institutions — including governments, health systems, and international bodies — to build climate resilience and coordinate adaptation or mitigation efforts, spanning health system governance, research and education, emergency management, and international development.

fields.name: k_interventions-measures-responses|4
fields.title: Policy
fields.description: Formal rules, regulations, and governance instruments designed by governments or international bodies to drive climate mitigation, adaptation, or resilience-building.

fields.name: k_interventions-measures-responses|5
fields.title: Technology / infrastructure
fields.description: Physical systems, equipment, and built infrastructure deployed to address environmental, social, or economic challenges, including systems designed to reduce emissions, improve resilience, or support service delivery.

fields.name: dsny000097_sub|0
fields.title: Adaptation behaviours
fields.description: Deliberate actions taken by individuals or communities to reduce exposure or vulnerability to climate-related hazards and protect health and livelihoods.

fields.name: dsny000097_sub|1
fields.title: Mitigation behaviours
fields.description: Voluntary or encouraged changes in individual and household behaviour that reduce greenhouse gas emissions across key consumption domains.

fields.name: dsny000098_sub|0
fields.title: Civic engagement
fields.description: Participation in collective and political processes aimed at influencing climate policy, community resilience planning, or social responses to climate hazards.

fields.name: dsny000098_sub|1
fields.title: Household protection
fields.description: Actions taken at the household level to reduce exposure to hazards or improve living conditions, such as installing insulation, flood barriers, ventilation, or emergency preparedness measures.

fields.name: dsny000098_sub|2
fields.title: Learning
fields.description: Acquiring knowledge and skills that enable individuals and communities to understand risks, make informed decisions, and adapt their behaviours and livelihoods accordingly.

fields.name: dsny000098_sub|3
fields.title: Lifestyle change in place
fields.description: Changes to daily routines, work patterns, or living arrangements made within a person's current location in response to changing conditions, without relocating.

fields.name: dsny000098_sub|4
fields.title: Migration
fields.description: Movement of individuals or communities away from areas made uninhabitable or highly hazardous by climate change, including both voluntary relocation and forced displacement.

fields.name: dsny000098_sub|5
fields.title: Other behaviour related to adaptation
fields.description: Adaptation behaviours not classified under the specific categories of civic engagement, psychological coping, household protection, learning, lifestyle change in place, migration, or self-protection.

fields.name: dsny000098_sub|6
fields.title: Psychological coping
fields.description: Psychological strategies and mental health practices that individuals use to manage stress, anxiety, and trauma associated with climate change and climate-related disasters.

fields.name: dsny000098_sub|7
fields.title: Self-protection
fields.description: Individual actions taken to protect personal health from climate hazards, such as using sunscreen, staying hydrated during heat events, or wearing respiratory protection during wildfires.

fields.name: dsny000107_sub|0
fields.title: Behaviour related to food/diet
fields.description: Changes in dietary patterns and food purchasing behaviour, such as reducing meat intake, minimising food waste, or choosing locally produced food, to lower the environmental footprint of food consumption.

fields.name: dsny000107_sub|1
fields.title: Behaviour related to goods/consumption/services
fields.description: Reductions or shifts in the purchase and use of physical goods and services to lower associated environmental impacts, including buying less, repairing, reusing, or choosing lower-impact products and services.

fields.name: dsny000107_sub|2
fields.title: Behaviour related to households
fields.description: Actions taken at the household level to reduce energy consumption and associated emissions, including reducing heating and cooling use, improving insulation, and adopting lower-emission energy sources.

fields.name: dsny000107_sub|3
fields.title: Behaviour related to mobility
fields.description: Behavioural changes in how individuals travel and commute, such as switching to public transport, cycling, walking, or reducing vehicle use, to reduce transport-related emissions.

fields.name: dsny000107_sub|4
fields.title: Other behaviour related to mitigation
fields.description: Mitigation behaviours not classified under the specific categories of mobility, household, food and diet, or goods and consumption.

fields.name: dsny000588_sub|0
fields.title: Community-based adaptation
fields.description: Locally designed and led responses to climate-health risks, drawing on community knowledge and priorities to develop contextually appropriate adaptation strategies.

fields.name: dsny000588_sub|1
fields.title: Cultural identity
fields.description: Culturally grounded practices, knowledge systems, and identities that support individual and community wellbeing, including indigenous-led approaches and the preservation of connections to land and heritage.

fields.name: dsny000588_sub|2
fields.title: Land / resource rights
fields.description: The legal and customary rights of communities and indigenous peoples to access, use, and govern land and natural resources, underpinning livelihood security and self-determination.

fields.name: dsny000588_sub|3
fields.title: Participatory governance
fields.description: Processes that involve communities in decision-making and planning, ensuring local voices shape policies, programmes, and strategies that affect them.

fields.name: dsny000588_sub|4
fields.title: Social cohesion / mutual aid
fields.description: Community networks and informal support systems that enable mutual assistance during times of stress or shock, including food sharing, community care, and grassroots first response.

fields.name: dsny000588_sub|5
fields.title: Z_Other community-based interventions
fields.description: Community-based interventions not classified under community-based adaptation, participatory governance, social cohesion, cultural identity, or land and resource rights.

fields.name: dsny000113_sub|0
fields.title: Coastal / marine protection
fields.description: Conservation and restoration of coastal and marine ecosystems including mangroves, coral reefs, and wetlands, providing storm surge protection, food security, flood buffering, and wellbeing co-benefits.

fields.name: dsny000113_sub|1
fields.title: Forest / land management
fields.description: Sustainable management and restoration of forests and land, including wildfire prevention, reforestation, agroforestry, peatland restoration for biodiversity and carbon sequestration, regenerative agriculture for soil health and food security, and ecological approaches to reducing disease vector habitat.

fields.name: dsny000113_sub|2
fields.title: Urban green-blue infrastructure
fields.description: Parks, street trees, green corridors, and urban water bodies that reduce heat island effects, support mental health, and increase urban resilience through ecosystem services.

fields.name: dsny000113_sub|3
fields.title: Z_Other ecosystem-based interventions
fields.description: Ecosystem-based interventions not classified under urban green-blue infrastructure, coastal and marine protection, or forest and land management.

fields.name: dsny000114_sub|0
fields.title: Emergency / disaster management
fields.description: Systems and institutions for preparedness, response, and recovery in relation to emergencies and disasters, including early warning, evacuation planning, and surge capacity for acute events.

fields.name: dsny000114_sub|1
fields.title: Health system governance
fields.description: Institutional actions to design and strengthen health systems for climate resilience, including decentralisation, workforce and capacity building in climate-sensitive disease, updating clinical guidelines for climate risks, and ensuring flood, heat, and storm resilience of health facilities and supply chains.

fields.name: dsny000114_sub|2
fields.title: International development / aid
fields.description: International funding, technical assistance, and development programmes directed at lower-income countries to support economic development, institutional capacity, and service delivery.

fields.name: dsny000114_sub|3
fields.title: Research / knowledge systems / education
fields.description: Research infrastructure, knowledge translation systems, and educational programmes that build understanding of risks and promote evidence-informed decision-making and behaviour change at individual or community level.

fields.name: dsny000114_sub|4
fields.title: Z_Other institution-based interventions
fields.description: Institutional interventions not classified under health system governance, research and education, emergency management, or international development and aid.

fields.name: dsny000087_sub|0
fields.title: Fiscal / incentive policy
fields.description: Market-based and fiscal mechanisms such as carbon taxes, emissions trading schemes, and subsidies used to incentivise emissions reductions or climate adaptation investments.

fields.name: dsny000087_sub|1
fields.title: Health-in-all-policies
fields.description: A governance approach that systematically integrates health considerations into climate policy and climate considerations into health policy, recognising that health outcomes are shaped by decisions made across multiple sectors including energy, transport, food, and land use.

fields.name: dsny000087_sub|2
fields.title: International / multilateral agreements
fields.description: Formal binding or non-binding agreements between nations or organisations to coordinate action on climate change, including treaties, protocols, and multilateral accords, e.g. UNFCCC mechanisms, Paris Agreement, WHO frameworks.

fields.name: dsny000087_sub|3
fields.title: National / subnational policy
fields.description: Institutional frameworks, strategies, and targets that guide governments and organisations in planning and implementing climate action, including national determined contributions, national adaptation plans and climate plans (e.g. land use policy, city-level climate health strategies, spatial planning, urban heat island reduction, flood plain management), surveillance and early-warning policy (mandated disease surveillance, heat alert systems), climate-change related public health information and education.

fields.name: dsny000087_sub|4
fields.title: Regulatory / legislative policy
fields.description: Legally binding rules, standards, and enforcement mechanisms that mandate emissions reductions, land use changes, or other climate-related behaviours by governments, industries, or individuals. E.g. emissions standards, environmental health regulations, fossil fuel bans.

fields.name: dsny000093_sub|0
fields.title: Adaptation technologies / infractstructure
fields.description: Technologies and built infrastructure designed to reduce vulnerability to climate impacts, including flood defences, heat-resilient buildings, and early warning systems.

fields.name: dsny000093_sub|1
fields.title: Emitting technologies / infrastructure
fields.description: Technologies and infrastructure that generate significant greenhouse gas emissions, whose phase-out or retrofitting is central to climate mitigation strategies. Covers so-called brown technologies.

fields.name: dsny000093_sub|2
fields.title: Mitigation technologies / infrastructure
fields.description: Technologies and infrastructure designed to reduce or eliminate greenhouse gas emissions.

fields.name: dsny000095_sub|0
fields.title: Adaptive built environment
fields.description: Built environment designs and retrofits that reduce heat exposure and improve thermal comfort, including cool roofs, reflective surfaces, passive cooling design, and heat-resilient housing construction.

fields.name: dsny000095_sub|1
fields.title: Climate-resilient water / sanitation
fields.description: Water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) infrastructure designed to remain functional under changing precipitation patterns, including flood-proof and drought-resilient water supply systems and sanitation systems adapted to climate variability.

fields.name: dsny000095_sub|2
fields.title: Coastal / flood defence
fields.description: Physical infrastructure protecting coastal and flood-prone communities from climate-related inundation, including sea walls, improved drainage systems, and managed retreat programmes that reduce population exposure.

fields.name: dsny000095_sub|3
fields.title: Digital / data-based technology / infrastructure
fields.description: Digital tools and data infrastructure supporting climate-health surveillance and response, including remote sensing, climate-health surveillance platforms, vector surveillance systems, and early warning and forecasting systems for climate-sensitive health risks.

fields.name: dsny000095_sub|4
fields.title: Food security technology
fields.description: Technologies that maintain food availability and safety under a changing climate, including drought-resistant crop varieties and cold chain systems that preserve food safety under warming conditions.

fields.name: dsny000095_sub|5
fields.title: Other adaptation technologies / infrastructure
fields.description: Adaptation technologies and infrastructure not classified under the specific categories of water and sanitation, built environment, digital systems, food security, or coastal and flood defence.

fields.name: dsny000096_sub|0
fields.title: Carbon-intensive built environment
fields.description: Buildings with poor insulation or energy performance that rely on fossil fuel heating and cooling systems, contributing to both emissions and energy poverty.

fields.name: dsny000096_sub|1
fields.title: Fossil fuel-based energy systems
fields.description: Power generation infrastructure using coal, oil, or gas combustion, associated with significant greenhouse gas emissions and air pollution health burdens.

fields.name: dsny000096_sub|2
fields.title: High-emission agricultural infrastructure
fields.description: Agricultural systems with high greenhouse gas footprints, including intensive livestock operations, synthetic fertiliser supply chains, and irrigation systems with large energy demands.

fields.name: dsny000096_sub|3
fields.title: Industrial / extractive infrastructure
fields.description: Mining, cement, steel, chemical, and other extractive and heavy industrial processes associated with high greenhouse gas emissions and direct health burdens from air, water, and soil pollution.

fields.name: dsny000096_sub|4
fields.title: Internal combustion transport infrastructure
fields.description: Road networks and vehicle fleets designed around internal combustion engines, generating traffic-related air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions with well-documented health impacts.

fields.name: dsny000096_sub|5
fields.title: Waste infrastructure with high emissions
fields.description: Waste disposal systems including landfills and open burning that generate methane and toxic air pollutants, contributing to both climate forcing and direct health harm.

fields.name: dsny000096_sub|6
fields.title: Z_Other emitting technologies / infrastructure
fields.description: Emitting technologies and infrastructure not classified under the specific categories of energy, transport, agriculture, built environment, industrial, or waste systems.

fields.name: dsny000094_sub|0
fields.title: Carbon capture
fields.description: Engineered systems that capture CO₂ from point sources or directly from the atmosphere and store it permanently, including carbon capture and storage (CCS) and direct air capture technologies.

fields.name: dsny000094_sub|1
fields.title: Clean energy systems
fields.description: Technologies and infrastructure for producing and distributing energy from low- or zero-carbon sources, including renewable energy systems, household energy access, cookstove replacement reducing indoor air pollution and emissions, and smart grid optimisation.

fields.name: dsny000094_sub|2
fields.title: Energy-efficiency
fields.description: Technologies and infrastructure that reduce energy consumption, including energy-efficient appliances, green buildings, housing insulation, and retrofits that reduce heating and cooling energy demand.

fields.name: dsny000094_sub|3
fields.title: Low-emission transport
fields.description: Infrastructure and systems enabling low-emission travel and transport, including active travel networks, electric vehicle charging infrastructure, and public transit systems.

fields.name: dsny000094_sub|4
fields.title: Sustainable food systems
fields.description: Low-emission agricultural technologies and food production systems, including plant-based food production, sustainable land management, and infrastructure for reducing food loss and waste.

fields.name: dsny000094_sub|5
fields.title: Waste management / circular economy
fields.description: Sanitation and waste management systems that reduce methane emissions and disease vectors, including circular economy approaches that minimise waste generation and improve resource recovery.

fields.name: dsny000094_sub|6
fields.title: Z_Other mitigation technologies / infrastructure
fields.description: Mitigation technologies and infrastructure not classified under the specific categories of clean energy, transport, energy efficiency, food systems, waste management, or carbon capture.

fields.name: k_sectors|0
fields.title: Agriculture / fishing / forestry (Sector)
fields.description: The sector encompassing crop cultivation, livestock rearing, aquaculture, fishing, and forest management.

fields.name: k_sectors|1
fields.title: Buildings / housing (Sector)
fields.description: The sector covering residential and commercial buildings, housing provision, and construction.

fields.name: k_sectors|2
fields.title: Education (Sector)
fields.description: The sector encompassing formal and informal education systems, including schools, universities, and vocational institutions.

fields.name: k_sectors|3
fields.title: Energy/Extractives (Sector)
fields.description: The sector covering electricity generation, fuel production, and resource extraction, including both fossil fuel and renewable energy systems.

fields.name: k_sectors|4
fields.title: Finance (Sector)
fields.description: The sector encompassing banking, insurance, investment, and financial services, including public and private finance mechanisms.

fields.name: k_sectors|5
fields.title: Healthcare (Sector)
fields.description: The sector providing medical care, public health services, and health infrastructure, including hospitals, primary care, and preventive health services.

fields.name: k_sectors|6
fields.title: Industry / trade / services (Sector)
fields.description: The sector encompassing manufacturing, retail, wholesale trade, and commercial services.

fields.name: k_sectors|7
fields.title: Information and communications technologies (Sector)
fields.description: The sector covering telecommunications, digital infrastructure, and information technology, including hardware, software, and connectivity systems.

fields.name: k_sectors|8
fields.title: Military (Sector)
fields.description: The military sector is the part of a country’s economy and government responsible for producing, organizing, and maintaining armed forces and defense capabilities, including personnel, equipment, operations, and infrastrucutre.

fields.name: k_sectors|9
fields.title: Public administration (Sector)
fields.description: The sector encompassing government agencies, civil services, and public institutions responsible for policy-making, regulation, and the delivery of public services in the context of climate change.

fields.name: k_sectors|10
fields.title: Social protection (Sector)
fields.description: The sector providing social safety nets, welfare services, and support systems that protect vulnerable populations from economic and social risks.

fields.name: k_sectors|11
fields.title: Transportation (Sector)
fields.description: The sector covering road, rail, air, and maritime transport systems, including infrastructure, vehicles, and logistics operations.

fields.name: k_sectors|12
fields.title: Water / sanitation / waste management (Sector)
fields.description: The sector responsible for water supply, sewage treatment, and solid waste management.

fields.name: k_actors|0
fields.title: Civil society (Actor)
fields.description: Non-profit organisations, advocacy groups, and community-based organisations that represent public interests, support communities, and hold governments and businesses accountable.

fields.name: k_actors|1
fields.title: Governments (Actor)
fields.description: National, regional, and local government bodies responsible for setting policy, enacting legislation, and implementing programmes within their jurisdictions.

fields.name: k_actors|2
fields.title: Households / individuals (Actor)
fields.description: Individual people and domestic units whose everyday choices, behaviours, and circumstances make them both agents of and subjects of wider social and environmental change.

fields.name: k_actors|3
fields.title: Private sector (Actor)
fields.description: Commercial enterprises, industries, and business associations whose operations, investments, and innovations shape economic and environmental outcomes.

fields.name: k_actors|4
fields.title: Supranational and international organizations (Actor)
fields.description: Supranational bodies including United Nations agencies, multilateral development banks, and intergovernmental organisations that coordinate policy, financing, and action across nations.

fields.name: k_governance-scale|0
fields.title: Global (Governance scale)
fields.description: The highest level of governance, encompassing worldwide institutions, agreements, and processes that operate across all nations.

fields.name: k_governance-scale|1
fields.title: International - multi-country (Governance scale)
fields.description: Governance arrangements and interventions involving a defined group of countries acting together across national boundaries, such as bilateral partnerships or plurilateral coalitions, without necessarily sharing a geographic region or formal institutional structure.

fields.name: k_governance-scale|2
fields.title: International - regional (Governance scale)
fields.description: Governance operating at a regional geographic scale spanning multiple countries within a formally defined geographic or institutional bloc, such as the European Union or the African Union.

fields.name: k_governance-scale|3
fields.title: National (Governance scale)
fields.description: Governance and policy implemented at the level of a single sovereign nation, including national legislation, strategic plans, and government-led programmes.

fields.name: k_governance-scale|4
fields.title: Sub-national - local / municipal (Governance scale)
fields.description: Governance at the local or municipal level, including city councils and district authorities responsible for planning, service delivery, and local policy implementation.

fields.name: k_governance-scale|5
fields.title: Sub-national - regional (Governance scale)
fields.description: Governance at the level of regions or provinces within a single country, such as states, counties, or devolved administrations with defined policy responsibilities.

fields.name: k_governance-scale|6
fields.title: Z_Household / individual (Governance scale)
fields.description: The smallest unit of governance scale, referring to decisions and actions taken by individual people or households.

fields.name: k_human-settlements|0
fields.title: Formal urban settlements
fields.description: Planned, officially recognised urban areas with functioning administrative systems, legal land tenure, and access to infrastructure and services, categorised by population size following Revi et al. (2025).

fields.name: k_human-settlements|1
fields.title: Informal settlements
fields.description: Residential areas characterised by lack of secure land tenure, inadequate infrastructure, poor access to basic services such as water, sanitation, and healthcare, and overcrowding. This category is intentionally broad, encompassing the diverse forms of unplanned or unauthorised settlement that develop on the periphery of formal cities, without relying on contested administrative labels that vary by country.

fields.name: k_human-settlements|2
fields.title: Peri-urban settlements
fields.description: Areas at the urban-rural interface characterised by mixed land use, rapid demographic and physical change, and often partial or transitional access to urban services. The term is used variably across research traditions to describe either the rural-urban fringe of a growing city or areas that are administratively rural but functionally urban.

fields.name: dsny000505_sub|0
fields.title: Cities
fields.description: Formal urban settlements with a population of between 100,000 and 1,000,000 inhabitants, with established administrative systems, diverse economies, and relatively comprehensive urban infrastructure.

fields.name: dsny000505_sub|1
fields.title: Megacities
fields.description: Formal urban settlements with a population exceeding 10,000,000 inhabitants, presenting unique challenges for governance, infrastructure, environmental management, and health system capacity.

fields.name: dsny000505_sub|2
fields.title: Million-cities
fields.description: Formal urban settlements with a population of between 1,000,000 and 10,000,000 inhabitants, characterised by complex governance structures, significant economic output, and high population density.

fields.name: dsny000505_sub|3
fields.title: Towns
fields.description: Formal urban settlements with a population of fewer than 100,000 inhabitants, typically characterised by local administrative functions, mixed economies, and partial urban service provision.

fields.name: dsny000511_sub|0
fields.title: Refugee / displaced settlements
fields.description: Settlements established to house populations forcibly displaced by conflict, persecution, or disaster, including formal refugee camps, informal displaced person settlements, and spontaneous settlements in host communities. Distinct from other informal settlements in their governance structures, legal frameworks, humanitarian actors, and policy context, and complementary to concepts of forced displacement and migration by capturing the physical and administrative character of where displaced people live rather than the movement itself.

fields.name: dsny000511_sub|1
fields.title: Slums / favelas
fields.description: Dense informal urban settlements characterised by substandard housing, insecure tenure, limited access to clean water and sanitation, overcrowding, and social marginalisation, known by varied local names including favelas, bidonvilles, katchi abadis, and shanty towns.

fields.name: dsny000511_sub|2
fields.title: Z_Other informal settlements
fields.description: Informal settlements not classified as slums, favelas, or refugee and displaced settlements, including other forms of unplanned or unauthorised housing such as illegal subdivisions, informal extensions of formal areas, and transitional settlements.

fields.name: k_geographic-location|0
fields.title: Africa (example)
fields.description: Africa is the world's second-largest continent by area and population, comprising 54 sovereign countries on a single landmass connected to Asia via the Sinai Peninsula, bordered by the Mediterranean Sea, Atlantic Ocean, Indian Ocean, and Red Sea.

fields.name: k_country-income|0
fields.title: High
fields.description: Countries classified by the World Bank as having the highest gross national income per capita, generally with the greatest adaptive capacity but also the highest historical contributions to cumulative emissions.

fields.name: k_country-income|1
fields.title: Low
fields.description: Countries classified by the World Bank as having the lowest gross national income per capita, typically facing the greatest climate vulnerability and least adaptive capacity.

fields.name: k_country-income|2
fields.title: Lower middle
fields.description: Countries classified by the World Bank in the lower-middle income tier, often experiencing rapid development while remaining highly vulnerable to climate-related health and economic impacts.

fields.name: k_country-income|3
fields.title: Upper middle
fields.description: Countries classified by the World Bank in the upper-middle income tier, with growing capacity for climate adaptation and mitigation but still facing significant climate risks.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|0
fields.title: Arid / semi-arid
fields.description: Regions characterised by low and variable rainfall, high evapotranspiration, and limited soil moisture, encompassing deserts, steppes, and dry shrublands where water scarcity is a primary constraint.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|1
fields.title: Boreal forest / taiga
fields.description: The world's largest terrestrial biome, spanning high-latitude northern regions and characterised by coniferous forest, cold winters, and short growing seasons, playing a major role in global carbon storage.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|2
fields.title: Coral reef
fields.description: Shallow marine ecosystems built by calcium carbonate-secreting corals, supporting exceptional biodiversity and coastal protection but highly vulnerable to ocean warming and acidification.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|3
fields.title: Delta / floodplain
fields.description: Low-lying landforms formed by sediment deposition at river mouths or along river corridors, characterised by high agricultural productivity and biodiversity but acute vulnerability to flooding, sea-level rise, and storm surge.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|4
fields.title: Desert
fields.description: Arid landscapes receiving very low annual precipitation, characterised by sparse vegetation and high temperatures, making them particularly vulnerable to heat stress and water scarcity.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|5
fields.title: Farmland
fields.description: Land used for agricultural production including arable crops, pasture, and mixed farming systems, representing a key interface between environmental conditions and food security.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|6
fields.title: Forest
fields.description: Land covered predominantly by trees and associated flora, providing critical ecosystem services including carbon sequestration, biodiversity habitat, and water regulation, all threatened by climate change.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|7
fields.title: Freshwater
fields.description: Inland water bodies including rivers, lakes, and streams, whose temperature, flow, and quality are sensitive to climate variability with consequences for drinking water and aquatic health.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|8
fields.title: Grassland / savanna
fields.description: Open landscapes dominated by grasses and low vegetation, sensitive to changes in precipitation and temperature, and at increased risk of drought and wildfire under climate change. Includes savanna (dominant in sub-Saharan Africa).

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|9
fields.title: Island
fields.description: Land masses surrounded by water, particularly small island developing states, which face existential threats from sea level rise, coastal erosion, and increased storm intensity.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|10
fields.title: Mangrove
fields.description: Coastal forest ecosystems dominated by salt-tolerant trees growing in intertidal zones of tropical and subtropical coastlines, providing habitat, carbon storage, and protection against storm surge and coastal erosion.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|11
fields.title: Mediterranean
fields.description: A climate zone and biome characterised by hot dry summers and mild wet winters, occurring around the Mediterranean Basin and analogous regions, with distinctive shrubland vegetation and high biodiversity.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|12
fields.title: Mountain
fields.description: Elevated terrain characterised by steep slopes and cooler temperatures, where glacier retreat, altered precipitation patterns, and biodiversity shifts are prominent climate change impacts.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|13
fields.title: Ocean / coastal
fields.description: Areas where land meets the sea, including coastlines, estuaries, and marine environments, highly exposed to sea level rise, storm surges, and ocean warming.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|14
fields.title: Peri-urban
fields.description: The transitional zone at the interface between urban and rural areas, characterised by mixed land use, rapid development, and populations that may lack full access to urban services while facing environmental pressures from adjacent cities.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|15
fields.title: Polar
fields.description: Cold, high-latitude environments at the Earth's poles, experiencing some of the fastest rates of climate warming globally, with consequences for sea ice, permafrost, and global sea levels.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|16
fields.title: Rainforest
fields.description: Dense tropical forests characterised by high biodiversity and rainfall, playing a critical role in global carbon cycling and increasingly threatened by deforestation and drought.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|17
fields.title: Riparian
fields.description: The transitional zone between terrestrial and aquatic environments along the banks of rivers, streams, and other watercourses, characterised by distinctive vegetation and sensitivity to flooding and drought.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|18
fields.title: Rural
fields.description: Sparsely populated areas outside urban centres, often reliant on agriculture and natural resources, and facing distinct climate risks including drought, flooding, and reduced service access.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|19
fields.title: Subtropical
fields.description: Regions located between the tropics and temperate zones, characterised by warm temperatures year-round, variable rainfall, and a mix of humid and dry subtropical climates.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|20
fields.title: Temperate
fields.description: Regions with moderate climates experiencing distinct seasons, where climate change is altering seasonal patterns, increasing extreme weather frequency, and affecting biodiversity.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|21
fields.title: Tropical
fields.description: Regions near the equator characterised by warm temperatures and high humidity year-round, where climate change is intensifying heat stress, vector-borne disease risk, and extreme rainfall.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|22
fields.title: Tundra
fields.description: A treeless biome found at high latitudes and elevations, characterised by permafrost, low vegetation, and extreme cold, with particular sensitivity to warming temperatures and permafrost thaw.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|23
fields.title: Urban
fields.description: Densely populated areas characterised by built infrastructure and high human activity, where urban heat island effects and air pollution amplify climate-related health risks.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|24
fields.title: Valley
fields.description: Low-lying areas between hills or mountains, often fertile and densely settled, which can be highly exposed to flooding and temperature extremes under climate change.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|25
fields.title: Wetland / peatland
fields.description: Low-lying ecosystems saturated with water, including marshes, swamps, and peatlands, which serve as important carbon stores and biodiversity habitats, threatened by drainage and climate change.

fields.name: k_health-exposure|0
fields.title: Air quality (Exposure)
fields.description: Exposure to outdoor or indoor air containing pollutants — including particulate matter, ozone, nitrogen dioxide, and wildfire smoke — at concentrations harmful to health.

fields.name: k_health-exposure|1
fields.title: Extreme weather events (Exposure)
fields.description: Acute exposure to extreme meteorological events — including floods, storms, cyclones, droughts, and wildfires — that cause direct physical harm or injury.

fields.name: k_health-exposure|2
fields.title: Food supply and safety (Exposure)
fields.description: Disruptions or changes to the availability, accessibility, and safety of food, including impacts on nutrition, foodborne pathogen risk, and agricultural productivity.

fields.name: k_health-exposure|3
fields.title: Heat stress (Exposure)
fields.description: Physiological strain placed on the body by elevated ambient temperature and humidity, impairing thermoregulation and increasing the risk of heat-related illness.

fields.name: k_health-exposure|4
fields.title: Social factors (Exposure)
fields.description: Social, economic, and structural conditions that mediate vulnerability to environmental hazards and shape health outcomes at individual and population level.

fields.name: k_health-exposure|5
fields.title: Ultraviolet / solar radiation (Exposure)
fields.description: Exposure to ultraviolet radiation from solar sources, associated with skin cancer risk, vitamin D synthesis, and immune modulation.

fields.name: k_health-exposure|6
fields.title: Vector distribution and ecology (Exposure)
fields.description: Changes in the geographic range, abundance, and seasonal activity of vectors — such as mosquitoes, ticks and mites — that alter the transmission risk of vector-borne diseases.

fields.name: k_health-exposure|7
fields.title: Water quality and quantity (Exposure)
fields.description: Changes in the availability, quality, and safety of freshwater and other water sources, including flooding, drought, and contamination affecting drinking water and sanitation.

fields.name: dsny000267_sub|0
fields.title: Housing quality / overcrowding (Exposure)
fields.description: Exposure to substandard, unsafe, or overcrowded living conditions that increase susceptibility to infectious disease, injury, and mental ill-health.

fields.name: dsny000267_sub|1
fields.title: Loss of livelihood / income (Exposure)
fields.description: Economic disruption resulting in the loss of employment, income, or livelihoods, with downstream effects on food security, mental health, and access to healthcare.

fields.name: dsny000267_sub|2
fields.title: Loss of place attachment / cultural identity (Exposure)
fields.description: Psychological and social harm arising from disruption to a sense of belonging, cultural heritage, and connection to land or community — particularly relevant to indigenous and displaced populations.

fields.name: dsny000267_sub|3
fields.title: Migration / forced displacement (Exposure)
fields.description: Involuntary or forced movement of populations away from their homes due to environmental, conflict, or economic pressures, with associated health and social consequences.

fields.name: dsny000267_sub|4
fields.title: Violence / conflict (Exposure)
fields.description: Exposure to interpersonal or collective violence, including armed conflict, gender-based violence, and civil unrest, as a determinant of physical and mental health outcomes.

fields.name: k_health-metrics|0
fields.title: Death (Metric)
fields.description: Metrics quantifying fatal health outcomes, including overall and cause-specific death rates across populations.

fields.name: k_health-metrics|1
fields.title: Disease burden / quality of life (Metric)
fields.description: Measures quantifying the non-fatal impact of disease on individuals and populations, including disease frequency, duration, and effect on functional status and wellbeing.

fields.name: k_health-metrics|2
fields.title: Exposure quantification (Metric)
fields.description: Metrics that quantify the magnitude of an exposure or the proportion of outcomes attributable to that exposure in a defined population.

fields.name: k_health-metrics|3
fields.title: Healthcare utilisation (Metric)
fields.description: Metrics quantifying the use of healthcare services, including primary, secondary, and emergency care, as indicators of health system demand and population health need.

fields.name: dsny000274_sub|0
fields.title: All-cause mortality (Metric)
fields.description: The rate of death from any cause within a defined population over a specified period, regardless of the underlying cause.

fields.name: dsny000274_sub|1
fields.title: Cause-specific mortality (Metric)
fields.description: The rate of death attributable to a specific disease, condition, or cause within a defined population.

fields.name: dsny000274_sub|2
fields.title: Excess / premature mortality (Metric)
fields.description: Deaths occurring earlier than expected relative to a baseline or reference population, or in excess of background mortality rates during a defined period or event.

fields.name: dsny000274_sub|3
fields.title: Infant / child mortality (Metric)
fields.description: Mortality rates among infants and children, typically measured as deaths per live births within specified age bands including neonatal, infant, and under-five periods.

fields.name: dsny000274_sub|4
fields.title: Maternal mortality (Metric)
fields.description: The death of a woman during pregnancy, childbirth, or within 42 days of delivery from causes related to or aggravated by the pregnancy or its management.

fields.name: dsny000274_sub|5
fields.title: Years of life lost (Metric)
fields.description: A measure of premature mortality calculated as the years of life lost due to death before a defined life expectancy threshold.

fields.name: dsny000281_sub|0
fields.title: Disability-adjusted life years (Metric)
fields.description: A summary measure of population health combining years of life lost to premature death (YLL) and years lived with disability (YLD), representing the total burden of disease.

fields.name: dsny000281_sub|1
fields.title: Health-related quality of life (Metric)
fields.description: Self-reported or assessed measures of physical, mental, and social functioning and wellbeing as affected by a health condition or its treatment.

fields.name: dsny000281_sub|2
fields.title: Incidence (Metric)
fields.description: The rate at which new cases of a disease or condition occur in a defined population during a specified time period.

fields.name: dsny000281_sub|3
fields.title: Prevalence (Metric)
fields.description: The proportion of a defined population living with a disease or condition at a specific point in time or during a defined period.

fields.name: dsny000281_sub|4
fields.title: Years lived with disability (Metric)
fields.description: A component of the Global Burden of Disease framework measuring the years of healthy life lost due to living with a non-fatal disease or disability, weighted by severity.

fields.name: dsny000293_sub|0
fields.title: Attributable fraction / risk (Metric)
fields.description: The proportion of disease cases or deaths in a population attributable to a specific exposure, estimating the potential reduction in burden if the exposure were eliminated.

fields.name: dsny000293_sub|1
fields.title: Relative risk / odds ratio (Metric)
fields.description: Statistical measures comparing the probability of a health outcome between exposed and unexposed groups, used to quantify the strength of association between an exposure and an outcome.

fields.name: dsny000287_sub|0
fields.title: Emergency department visit (Metric)
fields.description: The rate or number of attendances at emergency departments for acute assessment and treatment, used as an indicator of urgent health need.

fields.name: dsny000287_sub|1
fields.title: Healthcare access disruption (Metric)
fields.description: Interruptions to the availability or accessibility of healthcare services, resulting in delayed, reduced, or foregone care for affected populations.

fields.name: dsny000287_sub|2
fields.title: Hospital admission (Metric)
fields.description: The rate or number of patients admitted to hospital as inpatients for treatment, observation, or care related to a specific condition.

fields.name: dsny000287_sub|3
fields.title: Length of hospital stay (Metric)
fields.description: The duration of an inpatient hospital episode, used as a measure of disease severity, healthcare resource use, and patient recovery.

fields.name: dsny000287_sub|4
fields.title: Outpatient / primary care visit (Metric)
fields.description: The rate or number of non-emergency contacts with primary care or outpatient services, including general practice, specialist clinics, and community health settings.

fields.name: k_health-outcomes|0
fields.title: N.3.1 Mortality
fields.description: The occurrence of death as a health outcome, classified by cause, age group, and population to characterise the fatal burden of disease.

fields.name: k_health-outcomes|1
fields.title: N.3.2 Communicable, maternal, neonatal, and nutritional diseases
fields.description: The broad category of diseases caused by infectious agents or related to maternal, neonatal, and nutritional conditions, as defined in the GBD cause hierarchy.

fields.name: k_health-outcomes|2
fields.title: N.3.3 Non-communicable diseases
fields.description: Chronic, non-infectious diseases of long duration including cardiovascular, respiratory, metabolic, neurological, and neoplastic conditions.

fields.name: k_health-outcomes|3
fields.title: N.3.4 Injuries
fields.description: Physical harm to the body resulting from external causes, including unintentional injuries, self-harm, interpersonal violence, and conflict.

fields.name: dsny000296_sub|0
fields.title: Communicable, maternal, neonatal, and nutritional mortality
fields.description: Deaths attributable to communicable diseases, maternal conditions, neonatal disorders, and nutritional deficiencies.

fields.name: dsny000296_sub|1
fields.title: Non-communicable mortality
fields.description: Deaths attributable to non-communicable diseases, including cardiovascular, respiratory, metabolic, and neoplastic conditions.

fields.name: dsny000296_sub|2
fields.title: Total / all-cause mortality (Outcome)
fields.description: Deaths from any cause combined, used as an overall measure of fatal burden without attribution to a specific disease or condition.

fields.name: dsny000305_sub|0
fields.title: Infectious diseases mortality
fields.description: Deaths caused by infectious and parasitic diseases, including respiratory, enteric, vector-borne, and other infections.

fields.name: dsny000305_sub|1
fields.title: Maternal mortality
fields.description: Deaths among women during pregnancy, childbirth, or the postpartum period attributable to obstetric causes.

fields.name: dsny000305_sub|2
fields.title: Neonatal mortality
fields.description: Deaths occurring in the first 28 days of life, attributable to preterm birth, birth asphyxia, neonatal infection, and congenital conditions.

fields.name: dsny000305_sub|3
fields.title: Nutrition-related mortality
fields.description: Deaths attributable to nutritional deficiencies and undernutrition, including protein-energy malnutrition and micronutrient deficiency disorders.

fields.name: dsny000306_sub|0
fields.title: Enteric infections mortality
fields.description: Deaths attributable to enteric infections transmitted via contaminated food or water, including diarrhoeal diseases and typhoid.

fields.name: dsny000306_sub|1
fields.title: Neglected tropical diseases and malaria mortality
fields.description: Deaths caused by neglected tropical diseases and malaria, disproportionately affecting populations in low-income tropical settings.

fields.name: dsny000306_sub|2
fields.title: Other infectious diseases mortality
fields.description: Deaths from infectious diseases not classified under respiratory, enteric, or vector-borne categories, including meningitis, encephalitis, and vaccine-preventable infections.

fields.name: dsny000306_sub|3
fields.title: Respiratory infections mortality (including tuberculosis)
fields.description: Deaths caused by infections of the respiratory tract, including tuberculosis, pneumonia, and other lower and upper respiratory infections.

fields.name: dsny000298_sub|0
fields.title: Cardiovascular mortality
fields.description: Deaths attributable to diseases of the heart and circulatory system, including ischemic heart disease, stroke, and heart failure.

fields.name: dsny000298_sub|1
fields.title: Chronic respiratory diseases mortality
fields.description: Deaths attributable to chronic conditions of the respiratory tract, including chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and asthma.

fields.name: dsny000298_sub|2
fields.title: Diabetes and kidney diseases mortality
fields.description: Deaths attributable to diabetes mellitus and chronic kidney disease, which frequently co-occur and share common risk pathways.

fields.name: dsny000298_sub|3
fields.title: Injury-related mortality (drowning, fires, disasters, suicide, violence)
fields.description: Deaths resulting from injuries including drowning, fires, natural disasters, suicide, and interpersonal violence.

fields.name: dsny000298_sub|4
fields.title: Neoplasms mortality
fields.description: Deaths attributable to malignant and benign neoplasms across all anatomical sites.

fields.name: dsny000298_sub|5
fields.title: Other non-communicable diseases mortality
fields.description: Deaths attributable to non-communicable diseases not classified under the major NCD categories of cardiovascular, respiratory, neoplastic, or metabolic disease.

fields.name: dsny000314_sub|0
fields.title: Enteric infections
fields.description: Infections of the gastrointestinal tract transmitted via contaminated food or water, including diarrhoeal diseases, typhoid, and cholera.

fields.name: dsny000314_sub|1
fields.title: HIV/AIDS and sexually transmitted infections
fields.description: Infections transmitted through sexual contact or blood-borne routes, including HIV/AIDS and bacterial and viral sexually transmitted infections.

fields.name: dsny000314_sub|2
fields.title: Maternal and neonatal disorders
fields.description: Conditions arising during pregnancy, childbirth, or the neonatal period, including obstetric complications and disorders of the newborn.

fields.name: dsny000314_sub|3
fields.title: Neglected tropical diseases and malaria
fields.description: A diverse group of infectious diseases that disproportionately affect populations in tropical and subtropical low-income settings, including parasitic, bacterial, and viral conditions.

fields.name: dsny000314_sub|4
fields.title: Nutritional deficiencies
fields.description: Conditions arising from insufficient intake of macro- or micronutrients, including protein-energy malnutrition and deficiencies in key vitamins and minerals.

fields.name: dsny000314_sub|5
fields.title: Respiratory infections and tuberculosis
fields.description: Acute and chronic infections of the respiratory tract, including tuberculosis, pneumonia, and upper respiratory infections.

fields.name: dsny000314_sub|6
fields.title: Z_Other infectious diseases
fields.description: Infectious diseases not classified under respiratory, enteric, or vector-borne categories, including bacterial, viral, and prion conditions of diverse transmission routes.

fields.name: dsny000324_sub|0
fields.title: Diarrheal diseases
fields.description: Illness characterised by loose or watery stools, caused by a range of enteric pathogens and strongly associated with unsafe water, poor sanitation, and food contamination.

fields.name: dsny000324_sub|1
fields.title: Invasive Non-typhoidal Salmonella (iNTS)
fields.description: Severe systemic infection caused by non-typhoidal Salmonella serovars invading the bloodstream, predominantly affecting young children and immunocompromised individuals in low-income settings.

fields.name: dsny000324_sub|2
fields.title: Typhoid and paratyphoid
fields.description: Systemic bacterial infections caused by Salmonella Typhi and Salmonella Paratyphi, transmitted via contaminated food and water.

fields.name: dsny000324_sub|3
fields.title: Z_Other intestinal infectious diseases
fields.description: Intestinal infectious diseases not classified under diarrhoea, cholera, typhoid, or iNTS, including other bacterial, viral, and parasitic gut infections.

fields.name: dsny000325_sub|0
fields.title: Cholera
fields.description: An acute diarrhoeal illness caused by the bacterium Vibrio cholerae, typically transmitted through contaminated water and capable of causing rapid dehydration and death.

fields.name: dsny000315_sub|0
fields.title: HIV/AIDS
fields.description: Infection caused by the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), which progressively damages the immune system and, without treatment, leads to acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS).

fields.name: dsny000315_sub|1
fields.title: Sexually transmitted infections excluding HIV
fields.description: Infections transmitted primarily through sexual contact, excluding HIV, including syphilis, gonorrhoea, chlamydia, and other sexually transmitted pathogens.

fields.name: dsny000364_sub|0
fields.title: Maternal disorders
fields.description: Medical conditions and complications directly related to pregnancy and childbirth, including haemorrhage, hypertensive disorders, obstructed labour, and sepsis.

fields.name: dsny000364_sub|1
fields.title: Neonatal disorders
fields.description: Conditions originating in the perinatal period affecting newborns, including preterm birth, birth asphyxia, neonatal infections, and congenital anomalies.

fields.name: dsny000365_sub|0
fields.title: Maternal abortion and miscarriage
fields.description: The spontaneous or induced termination of pregnancy before viability, including miscarriage, unsafe abortion, and related complications.

fields.name: dsny000367_sub|0
fields.title: Low birth weight
fields.description: Birth weight below 2,500 grams, associated with increased neonatal mortality, infection susceptibility, and long-term developmental and metabolic risk.

fields.name: dsny000367_sub|1
fields.title: Neonatal preterm birth
fields.description: Birth occurring before 37 completed weeks of gestation, associated with increased risk of respiratory distress, infection, neurodevelopmental impairment, and neonatal death.

fields.name: dsny000330_sub|0
fields.title: African trypanosomiasis
fields.description: A vector-borne parasitic disease caused by Trypanosoma brucei, transmitted by tsetse flies, causing progressive neurological deterioration if untreated.

fields.name: dsny000330_sub|1
fields.title: Chagas disease
fields.description: A vector-borne parasitic disease caused by Trypanosoma cruzi, transmitted by triatomine bugs and endemic to Latin America, with chronic cardiac and digestive complications.

fields.name: dsny000330_sub|2
fields.title: Chikungunya
fields.description: A mosquito-borne viral disease transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, causing acute fever and severe joint pain that can persist for months.

fields.name: dsny000330_sub|3
fields.title: Cystic echinococcosis
fields.description: A zoonotic parasitic disease caused by the larval stage of Echinococcus granulosus tapeworm, producing fluid-filled cysts predominantly in the liver and lungs.

fields.name: dsny000330_sub|4
fields.title: Cysticercosis
fields.description: Infection by the larval stage of the pork tapeworm Taenia solium, which can invade the brain causing neurocysticercosis, a leading cause of acquired epilepsy.

fields.name: dsny000330_sub|5
fields.title: Dengue
fields.description: A mosquito-borne viral infection caused by dengue virus serotypes, transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, producing fever, severe headache, and in severe cases haemorrhagic complications.

fields.name: dsny000330_sub|6
fields.title: Ebola
fields.description: A severe and often fatal viral haemorrhagic fever caused by Ebola virus, characterised by fever, bleeding, and multi-organ failure.

fields.name: dsny000330_sub|7
fields.title: Food-borne trematodiases
fields.description: Parasitic infections caused by trematode flatworms acquired through consumption of contaminated raw or undercooked fish, crustaceans, or aquatic plants.

fields.name: dsny000330_sub|8
fields.title: Guinea worm disease
fields.description: A parasitic infection caused by Dracunculus medinensis, acquired by drinking water containing infected copepods, resulting in a slowly emerging worm through the skin.

fields.name: dsny000330_sub|9
fields.title: Intestinal nematode infections
fields.description: Parasitic worm infections transmitted through soil contaminated with faecal matter, including ascariasis, hookworm, and trichuriasis, causing malnutrition and developmental impairment.

fields.name: dsny000330_sub|10
fields.title: Leishmaniasis
fields.description: A parasitic disease caused by Leishmania species, transmitted by sandflies, presenting as cutaneous, mucocutaneous, or visceral forms.

fields.name: dsny000330_sub|11
fields.title: Leprosy
fields.description: A chronic bacterial infection caused by Mycobacterium leprae, affecting the skin, peripheral nerves, and mucous membranes, and historically associated with significant stigma.

fields.name: dsny000330_sub|12
fields.title: Leptospirosis
fields.description: A bacterial zoonosis caused by Leptospira species, transmitted through contact with water or soil contaminated by infected animal urine, with risk elevated during flooding events.

fields.name: dsny000330_sub|13
fields.title: Lymphatic filariasis
fields.description: A mosquito-transmitted parasitic disease caused by filarial worms, leading to lymphatic damage, lymphoedema, and disfiguring swelling of the limbs and genitals.

fields.name: dsny000330_sub|14
fields.title: Malaria
fields.description: A parasitic disease transmitted by Anopheles mosquitoes, caused by Plasmodium species, producing fever, anaemia, and potentially fatal cerebral complications.

fields.name: dsny000330_sub|15
fields.title: Onchocerciasis
fields.description: A parasitic disease caused by Onchocerca volvulus, transmitted by blackflies near fast-flowing rivers, causing skin disease and progressive visual impairment leading to blindness.

fields.name: dsny000330_sub|16
fields.title: Rabies
fields.description: A fatal viral encephalitis caused by lyssavirus, transmitted through the bite of infected animals, almost universally fatal once clinical symptoms develop.

fields.name: dsny000330_sub|17
fields.title: Schistosomiasis
fields.description: A parasitic disease caused by Schistosoma flatworms, transmitted through contact with contaminated freshwater, causing chronic inflammation of the bladder, liver, and intestines.

fields.name: dsny000330_sub|18
fields.title: Trachoma
fields.description: A chronic bacterial eye infection caused by Chlamydia trachomatis, the leading infectious cause of preventable blindness worldwide.

fields.name: dsny000330_sub|19
fields.title: Yellow fever
fields.description: An acute viral haemorrhagic disease transmitted by Aedes and Haemagogus mosquitoes, endemic in tropical Africa and South America.

fields.name: dsny000330_sub|20
fields.title: Zika virus
fields.description: A mosquito-borne viral infection caused by Zika virus, typically mild in adults but associated with congenital microcephaly and Guillain-Barré syndrome.

fields.name: dsny000330_sub|21
fields.title: Zz_Other neglected tropical diseases
fields.description: Neglected tropical diseases not classified under specific GBD sub-categories, including other parasitic and bacterial infections endemic to tropical regions.

fields.name: dsny000370_sub|0
fields.title: Childhood stunting and wasting
fields.description: Growth faltering in children due to chronic undernutrition (stunting: low height-for-age) or acute undernutrition (wasting: low weight-for-height), with serious consequences for development and survival.

fields.name: dsny000370_sub|1
fields.title: Dietary iron deficiency
fields.description: Insufficient dietary iron intake leading to iron deficiency anaemia, impairing oxygen transport, cognitive development, and immune function.

fields.name: dsny000370_sub|2
fields.title: Iodine deficiency
fields.description: Conditions resulting from insufficient dietary iodine, including goitre, hypothyroidism, and cretinism, with adverse effects on thyroid function and neurodevelopment.

fields.name: dsny000370_sub|3
fields.title: Protein-energy malnutrition
fields.description: Severe deficiency of protein and energy intake, manifesting as marasmus (energy deficiency) or kwashiorkor (protein deficiency), predominantly affecting young children in food-insecure settings.

fields.name: dsny000370_sub|4
fields.title: Vitamin A deficiency
fields.description: Deficiency of vitamin A resulting in night blindness, increased susceptibility to infection, and xerophthalmia, predominantly affecting children and pregnant women.

fields.name: dsny000370_sub|5
fields.title: Z_Other nutritional deficiencies
fields.description: Nutritional deficiency conditions not elsewhere classified, including deficiencies in zinc, folate, calcium, and other micronutrients essential for health.

fields.name: dsny000318_sub|0
fields.title: COVID-19
fields.description: Respiratory illness caused by the SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus, ranging from mild infection to severe pneumonia, acute respiratory distress, and multi-organ failure.

fields.name: dsny000318_sub|1
fields.title: Lower respiratory infections
fields.description: Infections of the lower respiratory tract including the lungs and bronchi, such as pneumonia and bronchiolitis, representing a leading cause of morbidity and mortality.

fields.name: dsny000318_sub|2
fields.title: Otitis media
fields.description: Infection and inflammation of the middle ear, commonly caused by bacterial or viral pathogens following upper respiratory infection.

fields.name: dsny000318_sub|3
fields.title: Tuberculosis
fields.description: A chronic bacterial infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, primarily affecting the lungs but capable of affecting any organ system.

fields.name: dsny000318_sub|4
fields.title: Upper respiratory infections
fields.description: Infections of the upper respiratory tract including the nose, throat, sinuses, and larynx, typically caused by viruses.

fields.name: dsny000353_sub|0
fields.title: Acute hepatitis
fields.description: Acute inflammatory liver disease caused by hepatitis A, B, C, D, or E viruses, ranging from self-limiting illness to fulminant hepatic failure.

fields.name: dsny000353_sub|1
fields.title: Diphtheria
fields.description: A vaccine-preventable bacterial infection caused by Corynebacterium diphtheriae, producing a toxin that causes a characteristic pharyngeal membrane and life-threatening airway obstruction and cardiac complications.

fields.name: dsny000353_sub|2
fields.title: Encephalitis
fields.description: Inflammation of the brain parenchyma caused by viral, bacterial, or autoimmune processes, presenting with altered consciousness, seizures, and focal neurological signs.

fields.name: dsny000353_sub|3
fields.title: Lyme disease
fields.description: A tick-borne bacterial infection caused by Borrelia burgdorferi, presenting with a characteristic expanding rash and potentially causing cardiac, neurological, and joint complications if untreated.

fields.name: dsny000353_sub|4
fields.title: Measles
fields.description: A highly contagious viral infection caused by measles morbillivirus, preventable by vaccination and causing fever, rash, and serious complications including pneumonia and encephalitis.

fields.name: dsny000353_sub|5
fields.title: Meningitis
fields.description: Inflammation of the meninges caused by bacterial, viral, or fungal pathogens, presenting with fever, headache, and neck stiffness and potentially fatal if untreated.

fields.name: dsny000353_sub|6
fields.title: Pertussis
fields.description: A highly contagious bacterial respiratory infection caused by Bordetella pertussis, characterised by severe paroxysmal coughing and particularly dangerous in infants.

fields.name: dsny000353_sub|7
fields.title: Tetanus
fields.description: A bacterial infection caused by Clostridium tetani toxin, producing painful muscle spasms and rigidity, with neonatal tetanus a particular risk in low-income settings.

fields.name: dsny000353_sub|8
fields.title: Varicella and herpes zoster
fields.description: Infection caused by varicella-zoster virus, producing chickenpox on primary infection and reactivating as herpes zoster (shingles) in older or immunocompromised individuals.

fields.name: dsny000353_sub|9
fields.title: Z_Other unspecified infectious diseases
fields.description: Infectious diseases not elsewhere classified, including rare, emerging, or unspecified infections not captured in major GBD sub-categories.

fields.name: dsny000377_sub|0
fields.title: Cardiovascular diseases
fields.description: Diseases of the heart and blood vessels, including ischemic heart disease, stroke, heart failure, and other circulatory conditions.

fields.name: dsny000377_sub|1
fields.title: Chronic respiratory diseases
fields.description: Long-term diseases affecting the airways and lung parenchyma, including obstructive, restrictive, and inflammatory conditions causing progressive respiratory impairment.

fields.name: dsny000377_sub|2
fields.title: Diabetes and kidney diseases
fields.description: A GBD grouping encompassing diabetes mellitus and kidney diseases, which share common metabolic risk factors and frequently co-occur.

fields.name: dsny000377_sub|3
fields.title: Digestive diseases
fields.description: Non-infectious diseases of the gastrointestinal tract and related organs, including the liver, gallbladder, and pancreas.

fields.name: dsny000377_sub|4
fields.title: Mental disorders
fields.description: Conditions characterised by clinically significant disturbances in cognition, emotion regulation, or behaviour, reflecting dysfunction in psychological or biological processes.

fields.name: dsny000377_sub|5
fields.title: Musculoskeletal disorders
fields.description: Diseases of bones, joints, muscles, and connective tissue, including osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, osteoporosis, and low back and neck pain.

fields.name: dsny000377_sub|6
fields.title: Neoplasms
fields.description: Diseases characterised by the uncontrolled growth of abnormal cells, including malignant cancers and benign tumours across all anatomical sites.

fields.name: dsny000377_sub|7
fields.title: Neurological disorders
fields.description: Diseases affecting the brain, spinal cord, and peripheral nervous system, including degenerative, inflammatory, and functional neurological conditions.

fields.name: dsny000377_sub|8
fields.title: Sense organ diseases
fields.description: Diseases affecting the organs of vision and hearing, including conditions causing visual impairment, blindness, and hearing loss.

fields.name: dsny000377_sub|9
fields.title: Skin and subcutaneous diseases
fields.description: Diseases affecting the skin and subcutaneous tissue, including inflammatory, infectious, allergic, and degenerative conditions.

fields.name: dsny000377_sub|10
fields.title: Substance use disorders
fields.description: Disorders characterised by compulsive use of psychoactive substances despite adverse consequences, including alcohol and drug use disorders.

fields.name: dsny000377_sub|11
fields.title: Z_Other non-communicable diseases
fields.description: Non-communicable diseases not classified under the major GBD NCD categories, including congenital, genitourinary, haematological, and other miscellaneous conditions.

fields.name: dsny000384_sub|0
fields.title: Aortic aneurysm
fields.description: Pathological dilation of the aortic wall with risk of rupture, most commonly involving the abdominal aorta and associated with hypertension and atherosclerosis.

fields.name: dsny000384_sub|1
fields.title: Atrial fibrillation and flutter
fields.description: Cardiac arrhythmias characterised by rapid and irregular electrical activity in the atria, associated with stroke risk and heart failure.

fields.name: dsny000384_sub|2
fields.title: Cardiomyopathy and myocarditis
fields.description: Diseases of the heart muscle including cardiomyopathy and inflammation of the myocardium, leading to impaired cardiac function and heart failure.

fields.name: dsny000384_sub|3
fields.title: Endocarditis
fields.description: Infection of the endocardium, most commonly involving the heart valves, caused by bacterial or fungal organisms and associated with significant morbidity and mortality.

fields.name: dsny000384_sub|4
fields.title: Hypertensive heart disease
fields.description: Structural and functional cardiac disease caused by chronic elevation of blood pressure, leading to left ventricular hypertrophy and heart failure.

fields.name: dsny000384_sub|5
fields.title: Ischemic heart disease
fields.description: Reduction in blood supply to the heart muscle due to atherosclerosis of the coronary arteries, presenting as angina, myocardial infarction, or sudden cardiac death.

fields.name: dsny000384_sub|6
fields.title: Lower extremity peripheral arterial disease
fields.description: Atherosclerotic obstruction of the arteries supplying the lower limbs, causing claudication, ischaemia, and risk of amputation.

fields.name: dsny000384_sub|7
fields.title: Non-rheumatic valvular heart disease
fields.description: Dysfunction of one or more heart valves not attributable to rheumatic disease, including aortic stenosis, mitral regurgitation, and degenerative valve conditions.

fields.name: dsny000384_sub|8
fields.title: Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension
fields.description: Elevated blood pressure in the pulmonary arterial circulation leading to progressive right heart failure and exercise limitation.

fields.name: dsny000384_sub|9
fields.title: Rheumatic heart disease
fields.description: Cardiac valve damage resulting from repeated episodes of rheumatic fever caused by group A streptococcal throat infection, predominantly affecting children and young adults in low-income settings.

fields.name: dsny000384_sub|10
fields.title: Stroke
fields.description: Sudden interruption or rupture of blood supply to the brain, causing focal neurological deficits, classified as ischaemic or haemorrhagic in type.

fields.name: dsny000384_sub|11
fields.title: Z_Other cardiovascular and circulatory diseases
fields.description: Cardiovascular and circulatory diseases not elsewhere classified in the GBD framework, including peripheral vascular conditions and miscellaneous cardiac disorders.

fields.name: dsny000397_sub|0
fields.title: Allergic rhinitis
fields.description: Allergic inflammation of the nasal mucosa triggered by inhaled allergens including pollen, dust mites, and moulds, causing sneezing, nasal congestion, and rhinorrhoea.

fields.name: dsny000397_sub|1
fields.title: Asthma
fields.description: A chronic inflammatory airway disease characterised by reversible bronchoconstriction, wheeze, and airway hyperresponsiveness, triggered by allergens, pollutants, and respiratory infections.

fields.name: dsny000397_sub|2
fields.title: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
fields.description: A progressive, non-reversible obstructive lung disease characterised by persistent airflow limitation, associated with tobacco smoke, indoor and outdoor air pollution, and occupational exposures.

fields.name: dsny000397_sub|3
fields.title: Interstitial lung disease and pulmonary sarcoidosis
fields.description: A heterogeneous group of diffuse parenchymal lung diseases characterised by inflammation and fibrosis of the lung interstitium, leading to progressive breathlessness and impaired gas exchange.

fields.name: dsny000397_sub|4
fields.title: Pneumoconiosis
fields.description: Occupational lung diseases caused by chronic inhalation of mineral or organic dusts, including silicosis, coal workers pneumoconiosis, and asbestosis.

fields.name: dsny000397_sub|5
fields.title: Z_Other chronic respiratory diseases
fields.description: Chronic respiratory diseases not captured under the specific GBD sub-categories of COPD, pneumoconiosis, asthma, or interstitial lung disease.

fields.name: dsny000438_sub|0
fields.title: Acute glomerulonephritis
fields.description: Acute inflammatory disease of the glomeruli, typically immune-mediated, presenting with haematuria, proteinuria, hypertension, and impaired renal function.

fields.name: dsny000438_sub|1
fields.title: Diabetes mellitus
fields.description: A group of metabolic diseases characterised by chronic hyperglycaemia resulting from defects in insulin secretion, insulin action, or both, with long-term damage to multiple organ systems.

fields.name: dsny000438_sub|2
fields.title: Kidney dysfunction
fields.description: Impaired kidney function assessed by reduced glomerular filtration rate or markers of renal damage, encompassing both chronic and acute kidney conditions.

fields.name: dsny000440_sub|0
fields.title: Acute kidney injury
fields.description: Sudden deterioration of kidney function over hours to days, causing accumulation of waste products and fluid imbalance, often associated with sepsis, dehydration, or nephrotoxic exposure.

fields.name: dsny000440_sub|1
fields.title: Chronic kidney disease
fields.description: Irreversible, progressive loss of kidney function over months to years, classified by stages of declining GFR and associated with cardiovascular risk and need for renal replacement therapy.

fields.name: dsny000404_sub|0
fields.title: Appendicitis
fields.description: Acute inflammation of the appendix, presenting with right iliac fossa pain and requiring surgical intervention to prevent perforation and peritonitis.

fields.name: dsny000404_sub|1
fields.title: Cirrhosis and other chronic liver diseases
fields.description: Progressive scarring and fibrosis of the liver resulting from chronic injury, including viral hepatitis, alcohol use, and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, ultimately causing liver failure.

fields.name: dsny000404_sub|2
fields.title: Gallbladder and biliary diseases
fields.description: Conditions affecting the gallbladder and bile ducts, including cholelithiasis, cholecystitis, and biliary obstruction.

fields.name: dsny000404_sub|3
fields.title: Inflammatory bowel disease
fields.description: Chronic immune-mediated inflammatory conditions of the gastrointestinal tract, including Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, characterised by relapsing intestinal inflammation.

fields.name: dsny000404_sub|4
fields.title: Inguinal, femoral, and abdominal hernia
